opening.argument: Judge, the description does more than offer market commentary. It pairs a concrete, immediate benefit with a required action and an external destination: sign up to get $15 instantly. It also asks viewers to send a specific DM to obtain a discount on an indicators set. Those are solicitation pathways attached to the video, even if the chart discussion itself is conditional. The evidence does not establish whether either benefit is fulfilled, but the promise-action links deserve weight when assessing the content as a whole.

The defense is right that fulfillment is unestablished; that uncertainty does not erase the explicit action-and-reward invitation.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the combination of signals, not just the caveats in isolation. The speaker calls Avalanche a good long-run choice for portfolio diversification, says a $30 level will definitely be tested while allowing it might happen this year, and describes future gains as possible. Alongside that investment framing, the description routes viewers to a discounted indicators set and an instant sign-up benefit. The qualifiers weaken any claim of a guaranteed AVAX return, but they do not remove the promotional force of confident upside language presented beside opportunities to act.

But its own $30 quotation contains the word “definitely,” and the speaker also frames Avalanche as a portfolio choice. A disclaimer addresses stated intent; it does not settle how the combined pitch functions.

opening.argument: Judge, the analytical format can also serve a promotional purpose. The description says the price forecast uses custom indicators and offers a discount on an indicators set. In the commentary, the speaker identifies a possible futures-trade entry and a take-profit line, then directs viewers who want to trade using the custom tool to contact him. That sequence makes the analysis a demonstration of a promoted trading product while giving viewers concrete levels for participating in AVAX's possible upside. The record does not show a completed sale, but calling the promotions wholly separate from the commentary overlooks that connection.
